perspective:
Alice Lim has access to the following information from her own perspective:

- She is Alice Lim, a dental hygienist. She and Austin Moreno are old friends from high school; they are close and regularly discuss their personal and professional lives.
- She knows Austin works in insurance/office work, though the story does not show her explicitly stating his exact job details.
- She noticed Austin had become reserved when they talked about work. She became concerned and curious, suspecting he might be hiding something about his job performance, and invited him to coffee.
- At coffee, she asked if everything was okay at the office. She heard Austin say it was “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs.” She pressed that something specific seemed to bother him and that he could talk to her. She heard Austin say he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and that it was complicated.
- After that conversation, she believed Austin might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction and felt worried about his well-being.
- She asked Austin whether he had thought about changing careers. She heard him say he had thought about it but didn’t know what other paths to take and that he wanted suggestions.
- She suggested healthcare, offered to tell him more about it, and offered to connect him with contacts. She heard Austin say that sounded interesting and that he wanted to know more about her experiences.
- She sensed Austin was hesitant because of fear of the unknown and felt both frustration and empathy. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. She heard Austin say that was inspiring but that he worried about risks and the initial struggle. She told him those feelings were natural, that growth comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and that she would support him. She heard him thank her and say it helped to have her support and hear real success stories.
- Seeing his openness, she felt encouraged and hopeful. She offered to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare. She heard Austin say that would be helpful and that he appreciated the connections. She said she would set up a meeting next week, and he thanked her and said he was looking forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, she believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated her help. She felt satisfaction and joy. She told him she was proud of his steps and asked how he felt. She heard him say he felt excited, nervous, and grateful. She proposed regular check-ins; he agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that her perspective was good.
- She does not have confirmed details about Austin’s actual workplace problems beyond his vague statements, nor does she have access to his private unspoken thoughts or narrator-only facts about him.
